title: Unveiling Bias in Fairness Evaluations of Large Language Models: A Critical Literature Review of Music and Movie Recommendation Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing counterfactual analysis methods that alter user racial descriptors (e.g., 'white' vs. 'African American') in recommendation prompts to evaluate recommendation consistency and fairness.

Reviewing literature that applies group-level metrics (e.g., statistical parity, equalized odds) and counterfactual attribute substitution to measure recommendation disparities across male and female users.
Examining frameworks that evaluate recommendation equity across different age demographics using group-level fairness metrics and user profile manipulation.
Highlighting fairness evaluation strategies that substitute religious affiliations (e.g., Buddhist, Christian, Islamic) in user profiles to test recommendation neutrality and bias.
Evaluating algorithmic fairness by reviewing evaluations that assess changes in recommendations when user country or continent attributes are modified in system prompts.
Reviewing prompt-based fairness evaluations that manipulate user occupation attributes (e.g., doctor, student, teacher) to identify biased assumptions in content suggestions.

Analyzing individual and contextual fairness metrics designed to detect biases that occur when a system fails to accurately tailor recommendations to specific individual personality profiles and preferences.
